correctness.rationale: The height \(d_f(x)\) of a strictly decreasing monotone map is nondecreasing with increments zero/one. \(D(x)=\sum_i d_{f_i}(x)\) falls by at least one along the join orbit and by exactly k at the final step, proving \(\nu(h)\le1+\sum_i(a_i-1)\). Join-distributivity shows its powers equal maxima of all words. Every extremal map on the minimal chain has join predecessor x-1; equality forces exactly one height jump at each \(x\ge2\), yielding a unique color word and reconstructing the maps. The inverse construction achieves the index for every prescribed tuple. Exhaustive program checks all ordered pairs for \(n\le8\), triples \(n\le5\), and quadruples \(n=4\); no extrapolation from finite tests is used.

value.rationale: A meaningful noncommutative refinement of an established nilpotent endomorphism semiring: it gives the sharp nilpotency index of the join and every possible mixed generator word from only the individual indices, shows equality for arbitrary index patterns, and classifies/counts ALL equality tuples on the smallest supporting chain. The multinomial counts are a natural sharp extremal invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice. It explains why common monotone height filtrations yield a strong sum rule without commuting generators, with concrete noncommuting extremizers.
